title: Classification of Imported and Export Goods
outcomes: Explain the structure of the Customs Tariff.

meta.exam_tip: Apply the rules in sequence and stop at the first rule that resolves classification.

concepts.title: Structure of the Customs Tariff
body: The First Schedule to the Customs Tariff Act, 1975 follows the Harmonized System: 21 sections and 98 chapters (97 HSN chapters plus India's Chapter 98 for special items like project imports). Codes are 8 digits in India against the 6-digit international level.
Each chapter has chapter notes with statutory force, then headings (4 digits), sub-headings (6 digits) and tariff items (8 digits). Columns show unit, standard rate and preferential rate.

The three General Explanatory Notes: dashes show the level of sub-classification; "%" means percentage of value under section 14; if no preferential rate is shown, the standard rate applies. The six General Rules for Interpretation (GRI) form part of the schedule and are applied in sequence.
concepts.work: One dash marks a first-level split of a heading; two dashes split that further.

concepts.title: Rules 1 and 2: legal text, incomplete goods and mixtures
body: Rule 1: section, chapter and sub-chapter titles are for reference only; legal classification follows the terms of headings and the related section or chapter notes. Notes of one chapter cannot be used to read another unless they say so.
Rule 2(a): a heading covering an article includes it in incomplete or unfinished form if it has the essential character of the finished article, and also unassembled or disassembled forms (CKD/SKD).
Rule 2(b): a reference to a material includes mixtures and combinations with other materials; goods of more than one material are classified under rule 3.
concepts.work: A car body shell without wheels still classifies as a car if it has its essential character.

concepts.title: Rules 3 to 6: competing headings, akin goods, containers
body: Rule 3(a): the most specific heading wins (an electric shaver under 8510 rather than domestic appliances 8509), but headings each covering only part of a composite good are equally specific. Rule 3(b): mixtures, composite goods and retail sets go by the component giving essential character, judged by nature, bulk, weight, value or role. Rule 3(c): if still undecided, the heading last in numerical order applies (Mahindra and Mahindra — 8704 over 8703).
Rule 4: goods not classifiable under the earlier rules go to the heading of goods they are most akin to, e.g. sun-control films treated like plastic blinds.

Rule 5(a): cases specially shaped for an article and suitable for long-term use are classified with it when presented together, unless the case gives the whole its essential character. Rule 5(b): normal packing goes with the goods, except packing clearly suitable for repeated use. Rule 6 limits comparison to sub-headings of equal rank within a heading.
concepts.analogy: Specific, then essential character, then the last heading.
concepts.work: A gift set of perfume and soap takes the classification of the item giving the set its character.

concepts.title: Parts and project imports
body: Parts suitable solely for a machine generally follow the machine's heading, but parts of general use (screws, springs) go to their own headings, and a separate parts heading takes priority where it exists, all subject to section and chapter notes.

Project imports under heading 9801 give one rate for all machinery, instruments, components and raw materials needed for initial setting up or substantial expansion of specified projects (industrial plants, irrigation, power and others), easing assessment of many diverse items.

Spares, raw materials and consumables up to 10% of the value of the specified goods may be imported under the project, subject to conditions such as contract registration. Individual exemption notifications can still apply to items under 9801.
concepts.analogy: Parts follow the machine unless they are general-use or have their own heading.
concepts.work: Bolts imported for a turbine are still classified as bolts.

model.title: General Rules for Interpretation

summary: Rule 1 headings and notes; Rule 2 incomplete and mixtures.
Rule 3: specific, essential character, last heading.
Rule 4 akin; Rule 5 cases and packing; Rule 6 same-level sub-headings.
remember: Three General Explanatory Notes: dashes, %, standard rate.

viva.model: Factors like nature, bulk, quantity, weight, value and the role of each component.
It holds special items such as project imports beyond the 97 HSN chapters.

viva.q: How are parts of general use classified?
viva.model: Under their own headings, separately from the machine they serve.

viva.q: What does a double dash before a description mean?
viva.model: A further split of the immediately preceding single-dash item.

viva.q: When does Rule 5(a) stop applying to a case?
viva.model: When the case itself gives the whole its essential character.
